Lighter Security Incident Update: Approximately 5M USDC Returned to Affected Trader, Withdrawals Resumed

Lighter said in its November 16 security incident report that an attacker exploited nonce reuse in unofficial signing code used by certain trading accounts to derive API private keys from public signatures. The attacker then created a public pool through a compromised account, transferred funds into the pool, and extracted assets by redeeming pool shares through an attacker-controlled account. Lighter confirmed that its protocol, smart contracts, infrastructure, and official SDKs were unaffected.

The incident triggered its smart contract-based Guardian mechanism, temporarily pausing withdrawals and allowing the Security Council to return approximately 5 million USDC to the affected trader. Withdrawals have since resumed, with pending requests being processed. Lighter has implemented wallet signature requirements for public pool transfers and made API key signatures non-public. It also plans to introduce IP allowlists, per-key permissions and limits, and proactively monitor and revoke API keys at risk from nonce reuse. — link

Trezor Says Shipping Partner Data Breach Exposed 27,000 Customer Orders

Trezor, a leading cryptocurrency hardware wallet manufacturer, disclosed that a breach at shipping partner Skladon exposed personal information linked to approximately 27,000 orders placed between August 9 and November 7. Skladon notified Trezor on November 15 that attackers had accessed its systems and were believed to have exported customer names, phone numbers, addresses, emails and order details. The breach affected multiple countries but not U.S. customers.
